senses.en: to suddenly move back in fear, horror, or disgust
(of a gun) to move backward when fired
the backward movement of a gun when fired

ex.en: She tends to recoil at the sight of spiders.
ex.zh: 她一看到蜘蛛就會往後縮。

root.note: 屁股往後退 → 退縮

senses.en: to remember something

ex.en: I can't recollect where I put my keys.
ex.zh: 我想不起來把鑰匙放在哪裡了。

root.note: 把記憶重新收集起來 → 回想

senses.en: able to be made consistent or brought into agreement

ex.en: Are economic growth and environmental protection reconcilable?
ex.zh: 經濟成長和環境保護可以兼顧嗎？

root.note: 可以再度和好的 → 可調和的

senses.en: to make a military observation of an area to gain information

ex.en: The captain sent two scouts to reconnoiter the enemy camp.
ex.zh: 上尉派了兩名偵察兵去偵察敵營。

root.note: 去重新認識地形 → 偵察（recon 是縮寫）

senses.en: to think again about a decision, especially in order to change it

ex.en: Please reconsider your decision to quit the team.
ex.zh: 請重新考慮你退出球隊的決定。

root.note: 再次考慮

senses.en: to build again after damage or destruction
to form an idea of a past event from evidence

ex.en: Police tried to reconstruct the events leading up to the crash.
ex.zh: 警方試圖還原車禍發生前的經過。

root.note: 再次建造 → 重建

senses.en: a source of help in a difficult situation
the use of something as a means of help

ex.en: Without a contract, the workers had no legal recourse.
ex.zh: 沒有合約，工人們在法律上求助無門。

parts.m: run 跑（在這個字裡拼成 cours）

root.note: 跑回去求助 → 求助的對象

senses.en: to return to a normal state of health or strength
to get back something lost or stolen

ex.en: It took him three weeks to recover from the flu.
ex.zh: 他花了三個星期才從流感中康復。

root.note: 把失去的取回 → 恢復

senses.en: cowardly; unfaithful to a duty or belief (archaic)
a coward or traitor

ex.en: The recreant knight fled the battle and abandoned his king.
ex.zh: 那個懦弱的騎士臨陣脫逃，拋棄了他的國王。

root.note: 收回誓言、背棄信仰 → 不忠的、懦弱的

senses.en: to make something again or reproduce it
[ˋrɛkrɪˏet] to refresh oneself through play or leisure

ex.en: The museum tried to recreate a typical Victorian kitchen.
ex.zh: 博物館試著重現典型的維多利亞時代廚房。

root.note: 再次創造 → 再現

senses.en: a return of something bad, such as a disease, after a period of inactivity

ex.en: Doctors feared a recrudescence of the fever in the spring.
ex.zh: 醫生擔心發燒在春天會復發。

root.note: 傷口再度流血 → 復發

senses.en: breaking out again after a period of inactivity

ex.en: Health officials tracked the recrudescent outbreak closely.
ex.zh: 衛生官員密切追蹤這波再度爆發的疫情。

root.note: 再度流血的 → 復發的

senses.en: to get someone to join a company, army, or group
a newly enlisted person

ex.en: The club hopes to recruit twenty new members this year.
ex.zh: 社團希望今年能招募二十名新成員。

root.note: 使（軍隊）再成長 → 招募

senses.en: to correct something that is wrong

ex.en: The company promised to rectify the billing error immediately.
ex.zh: 公司承諾立刻更正帳單錯誤。

root.note: 使變直、變正確 → 糾正

senses.en: morally correct behavior; honesty

ex.en: The senator was admired for his moral rectitude.
ex.zh: 那位參議員因道德上的正直而受人敬佩。

root.note: 行為筆直 → 正直

senses.en: to recover from illness or exhaustion
to get back money or losses

ex.en: She went to the countryside to recuperate after surgery.
ex.zh: 她手術後到鄉下休養。

parts.m: get, take 拿（拉丁文 capere）

root.note: 把健康拿回來 → 復原

senses.en: to happen again, especially repeatedly

ex.en: If the pain should recur, call your doctor.
ex.zh: 如果疼痛再次發生，請打給你的醫生。

root.note: 再跑回來 → 再發生

senses.en: to cure or heal again; to recover (archaic)

ex.en: In the old tale, only a magic herb could recure the wounded prince.
ex.zh: 在古老的故事裡，只有一種神奇草藥能治好受傷的王子。

root.note: 再次治療 → 治癒

senses.en: happening often or repeatedly

ex.en: Loneliness is a recurrent theme in her novels.
ex.zh: 孤獨是她小說中反覆出現的主題。

root.note: 一再跑回來的 → 反覆發生的

senses.en: the act of saving or being saved from sin or evil
the act of exchanging something for money or goods

ex.en: The film is a story of redemption about a man who rebuilds his life.
ex.zh: 這部電影講述一個男人重建人生的救贖故事。

root.note: 買回來 → 贖回、救贖

senses.en: a pleasant, strong smell

ex.en: The redolence of fresh bread filled the little shop.
ex.zh: 新鮮麵包的香氣瀰漫整間小店。

root.note: 散發出氣味 → 芬芳

senses.en: strongly reminiscent or suggestive of something
strongly smelling of something

ex.en: The old house was redolent of my grandmother's cooking.
ex.zh: 那棟老房子讓我想起祖母做菜的味道。

root.note: 散發氣味的 → 芬芳、令人聯想的

mn: 常見用法 be redolent of：充滿…的氣息、令人想起…。

senses.en: formidable, especially as an opponent; worthy of respect or fear
senses.zh: 令人敬畏的；可怕的（對手）

ex.en: She faced a redoubtable opponent in the chess final.
ex.zh: 她在西洋棋決賽中碰上一位令人畏懼的對手。

root.note: 非常值得害怕的 → 令人敬畏的

senses.en: to contribute to or have an effect on someone's credit or advantage
to come back upon someone as a result

ex.en: Her success will redound to the credit of the whole school.
ex.zh: 她的成功會為全校增光。

parts.m: wave, surge 波浪（拉丁文 unda）

root.note: 浪潮湧回來 → 影響回到某人身上

senses.en: to correct an unfair situation
money or action given to make up for a wrong

ex.en: The new law aims to redress the balance between workers and employers.
ex.zh: 新法旨在矯正勞資之間的失衡。

parts.m: set straight 擺正（古法文 dresser）

root.note: 再擺正 → 糾正

senses.en: able to be reduced or simplified to a smaller or simpler form
senses.zh: 可簡化的；可歸納的；可減少的

ex.en: Human behavior is not simply reducible to a few rules.
ex.zh: 人類行為不能單純簡化成幾條規則。

root.note: 可以帶回更簡單的形式 → 可簡化的

senses.en: the state of being more than needed; unnecessary repetition (usually redundancy)

ex.en: The editor cut every redundance from the long essay.
ex.zh: 編輯把長文中所有冗贅的地方都刪掉了。

root.note: 一直湧出 → 過多

senses.en: not needed; more than necessary
(British) no longer employed because the job is not needed

ex.en: The phrase "free gift" is redundant because all gifts are free.
ex.zh: free gift 這個詞是多餘的，因為禮物本來就是免費的。

root.note: 一直湧出來、過多的 → 多餘的

senses.en: to establish something again, such as a relationship or system

ex.en: The two countries hope to reestablish diplomatic relations.
ex.zh: 兩國希望恢復邦交。

root.note: 再次建立

senses.en: to mention or talk about someone or something
to look at something for information
to send someone to another person or place for help

ex.en: You may refer to your notes during the exam.
ex.zh: 考試時你可以查閱筆記。

root.note: 帶回去（給某人、某資料）→ 提及、參考

senses.en: able to be attributed or assigned to something

ex.en: The symptoms were referable to a problem in the spine.
ex.zh: 這些症狀可以歸因於脊椎的問題。

root.note: 可以歸於某處的

senses.en: an official who makes sure players follow the rules in a game
a person who gives a reference for a job applicant
to act as a referee

ex.en: The referee blew the whistle to stop the game.
ex.zh: 裁判吹哨停止比賽。

root.note: 爭議被提交給他的人 → 裁判

senses.en: a person or thing that refers someone to another, such as a website that sends visitors
senses.zh: 推薦者；轉介者；（網站）來源頁

ex.en: Each new customer's referrer receives a small discount.
ex.zh: 每位新顧客的推薦人都能得到一點折扣。

root.note: 轉介的人或來源

senses.en: a factory where substances such as oil or sugar are purified

ex.en: The oil refinery employs over a thousand workers.
ex.zh: 這座煉油廠僱用了超過一千名員工。

root.note: 把東西弄得更純的地方 → 精煉廠

senses.en: able to be reflected

ex.en: Only reflectible light can be seen bouncing off the mirror.
ex.zh: 只有可反射的光才能看到從鏡子上反彈出來。

root.note: 可以彎回去的 → 可反射的

senses.en: an image seen in a mirror or on a shiny surface
serious thought or consideration
a sign or result of something

ex.en: She saw her reflection in the calm lake.
ex.zh: 她在平靜的湖面上看到自己的倒影。

root.note: 光線彎回來 → 反射、倒影；思緒回轉 → 反省

senses.en: a piece of glass, metal, or plastic that reflects light

ex.en: Put a reflector on your bike so drivers can see you at night.
ex.zh: 在腳踏車上裝反光片，這樣晚上駕駛才看得到你。

root.note: 把光彎回去的東西

senses.en: capable of being reflected or bent back

ex.en: Early scientists debated whether heat rays were reflexible like light.
ex.zh: 早期科學家爭論熱射線是否像光一樣可以反射。

root.note: 可以彎回去的

senses.en: to make changes in something in order to improve it
a change made to improve something
to improve one's behavior

ex.en: Many people agree that we need to reform the tax system.
ex.zh: 許多人同意我們需要改革稅制。

root.note: 重新塑形 → 改革

senses.en: a person who works to make changes in society or politics

ex.en: The young reformer fought to improve conditions in city schools.
ex.zh: 這位年輕的改革者努力改善城市學校的狀況。

root.note: 推動改革的人

senses.en: (of water, glass, etc.) to make light change direction as it passes through

ex.en: A prism can refract white light into a rainbow of colors.
ex.zh: 稜鏡能把白光折射成彩虹般的顏色。

root.note: 把光打斷、轉彎 → 折射

senses.en: stubborn and difficult to control
(of a disease) not responding to treatment
resistant to heat

ex.en: The refractory mule refused to move another step.
ex.zh: 那頭倔強的騾子一步也不肯再走。

root.note: 打破（規矩）、頂回去 → 倔強的

senses.en: able to be refuted or disproved

ex.en: Even the professor admitted that her theory was refragable.
ex.zh: 就連教授也承認她的理論是可以被反駁的。

parts.m: vote, oppose 投票、反對（拉丁文 refragari）

root.note: 可以投反對票的 → 可反駁的

mn: 反義字 irrefragable（無可辯駁的）比較常見。

senses.en: the power of refracting light

ex.en: Diamond has a very high refringency, which makes it sparkle.
ex.zh: 鑽石的折射力很高，所以閃閃發光。

root.note: 使光折斷轉彎的能力 → 折射力

senses.en: refracting light; refractive

ex.en: The refringent crystal split the sunlight into bands of color.
ex.zh: 那塊有折射力的晶體把陽光分成一道道色帶。

root.note: 使光折斷轉彎的 → 折射的

senses.en: the act of saying or showing that one will not do or accept something

ex.en: His refusal to apologize made the situation worse.
ex.zh: 他拒絕道歉讓情況變得更糟。

root.note: 拒絕

senses.en: to prove a statement or theory to be wrong

ex.en: The scientist used new data to refute the old theory.
ex.zh: 那位科學家用新數據推翻了舊理論。

root.note: 打回去 → 駁斥

senses.en: to entertain or amuse someone with talk
to give someone plenty of food and drink

ex.en: Grandpa likes to regale us with stories of his travels.
ex.zh: 爺爺喜歡講他旅行的故事逗我們開心。

parts.m: pleasure, merriment 歡樂（古法文 gale）

root.note: 讓人非常開心 → 款待

senses.en: the emblems or special clothing of royalty or an official position
senses.zh: 王權標誌；正式禮服；徽章

ex.en: The graduates marched in full academic regalia.
ex.zh: 畢業生們穿著全套學位服行進。

root.note: 國王的物品 → 王權標誌

senses.en: the state of being royal; kingly dignity

ex.en: The actress played the queen with great regality.
ex.zh: 那位女演員把女王演得很有王者風範。

root.note: 國王的特質 → 王者風範

senses.en: (of a living thing) to grow new tissue or parts
to bring new life or energy to a place or system

ex.en: A lizard can regenerate its tail if it loses it.
ex.zh: 蜥蜴斷尾後可以再生。

root.note: 再次產生 → 再生

senses.en: a person who rules while a king or queen is too young, absent, or ill
a member of a governing board of a university

ex.en: The prince's uncle served as regent until the boy turned eighteen.
ex.zh: 王子的叔叔擔任攝政，直到男孩滿十八歲。

root.note: 代為統治的人 → 攝政者

senses.en: the killing of a king, or a person who kills a king

ex.en: The plot ended in regicide and years of civil war.
ex.zh: 那場陰謀以弒君告終，並引發多年內戰。

root.note: 殺國王 → 弒君

senses.en: a government, especially an authoritarian one
a system or ordered way of doing things

ex.en: The military regime banned all opposition parties.
ex.zh: 軍政府禁止所有反對黨。

root.note: 統治方式 → 政權

senses.en: a planned program of diet, exercise, or medical treatment
senses.zh: （飲食、運動、治療的）養生法；療程

ex.en: The athlete follows a strict training regimen.
ex.zh: 那位運動員遵循嚴格的訓練計畫。

root.note: 規範生活的方法 → 養生法

mn: regimen（養生計畫）、regime（政權）、regiment（軍團）長得很像要分清楚。

senses.en: a permanent unit of an army
[ˋrɛdʒəˏmɛnt] to organize or control strictly

ex.en: Her grandfather served in a cavalry regiment during the war.
ex.zh: 她的祖父戰時在騎兵團服役。

root.note: 受統轄的單位 → 軍團

senses.en: reigning; ruling in one's own right
currently having the greatest influence

ex.en: Victoria was a queen regnant, not merely the wife of a king.
ex.zh: 維多利亞是在位女王，而不只是國王的妻子。

root.note: 正在統治的

senses.en: to return to an earlier and less advanced state

ex.en: Without practice, your language skills may regress.
ex.zh: 不練習的話，你的語言能力可能會退步。

root.note: 往回走 → 倒退

senses.en: feeling or showing sadness or disappointment about something one did or did not do

ex.en: He gave a regretful smile and said he could not come.
ex.zh: 他露出遺憾的微笑，說自己沒辦法來。

root.note: 充滿悔意的

mn: regretful 形容人的感受；regrettable 形容事情令人遺憾。

senses.en: to help someone return to normal life after illness, injury, or prison
to restore something to good condition or a good reputation

ex.en: The program helps rehabilitate former prisoners through job training.
ex.zh: 這個計畫透過職業訓練幫助前受刑人重返社會。

root.note: 使再次有能力 → 復健

senses.en: the period during which a king or queen rules
to rule as a king or queen
to be the main or most noticeable quality

ex.en: The castle was built during the reign of Henry VIII.
ex.zh: 這座城堡建於亨利八世在位期間。

parts.m: kingdom, rule 統治（拉丁文 regnum）

root.note: 統治

mn: reign（統治）、rein（韁繩）、rain（雨）同音不同字。

senses.en: to repay someone for money they have spent

ex.en: The company will reimburse you for travel expenses.
ex.zh: 公司會幫你報銷差旅費。

root.note: 把錢放回錢包裡 → 償還

senses.en: a long strap used to control a horse
(reins) the power to control something
to control or restrain

ex.en: The government must rein in its spending.
ex.zh: 政府必須控制支出。

mn: rein in 控制；give free rein 放手讓人自由發揮。

senses.en: to restore someone to a former job or position
to bring back a law, rule, or practice

ex.en: The court ordered the company to reinstate the fired workers.
ex.zh: 法院命令公司讓被解僱的工人復職。

root.note: 再放回原來的狀態 → 復職

senses.en: to say something again, often for emphasis

ex.en: Let me reiterate that safety is our top priority.
ex.zh: 讓我再強調一次，安全是我們的第一優先。

parts.m: again 又一次（拉丁文 iterum）

root.note: 一次又一次地說 → 重申

senses.en: to join or return to a group or person again
[rɪˋdʒɔɪn] to say something in reply, especially sharply

ex.en: After his injury healed, he was able to rejoin the team.
ex.zh: 傷好之後，他得以重回球隊。

root.note: 再次加入；回話 → 反駁

senses.en: to make someone or something look or feel younger or more lively

ex.en: A week at the beach helped rejuvenate the tired family.
ex.zh: 在海邊待一週讓疲憊的一家人恢復了活力。

root.note: 使再次年輕 → 恢復活力

senses.en: the process of becoming young or vigorous again

ex.en: Spring brings a rejuvenescence to the whole forest.
ex.zh: 春天讓整片森林重新恢復生機。

root.note: 再度變年輕的過程

senses.en: a return to illness after a period of improvement
to return to a worse state or bad habit after improving

ex.en: The patient suffered a relapse after leaving the hospital.
ex.zh: 那位病人出院後病情復發。

root.note: 又滑回去 → 復發

senses.en: to move someone or something to a lower or less important position
senses.zh: 貶謫；降級；置於次要地位

ex.en: The new manager tried to relegate her to a desk job.
ex.zh: 新主管試圖把她貶去做內勤工作。

root.note: 派到遠處去 → 貶謫

senses.en: to finally agree to something after refusing
to become less severe or intense

ex.en: Her parents finally agreed to relent and let her go to the concert.
ex.zh: 她的父母終於讓步，讓她去聽演唱會。

parts.m: slow, soft 慢、軟（拉丁文 lentus）

root.note: 軟化下來 → 讓步

mn: relentless（不停的、無情的）就是「不肯 relent」。

senses.en: closely connected or appropriate to the matter at hand

ex.en: Please include only relevant information in your report.
ex.zh: 請在報告中只放相關的資訊。

root.note: 被舉出來協助說明的 → 相關的

senses.en: dependence on or trust in someone or something

ex.en: Our reliance on smartphones keeps growing every year.
ex.zh: 我們對智慧型手機的依賴逐年增加。

root.note: 依靠

senses.en: dependent on someone or something

ex.en: The island is heavily reliant on tourism.
ex.zh: 這座島非常依賴觀光業。

root.note: 依靠的

senses.en: to give up something, often unwillingly

ex.en: The old king refused to relinquish power.
ex.zh: 老國王拒絕交出權力。

root.note: 留下離開 → 放棄

senses.en: a container for holy relics

ex.en: The golden reliquary is said to hold a bone of the saint.
ex.zh: 據說那個金色聖骨匣裡存放著聖人的一塊骨頭。

root.note: 裝遺物的容器 → 聖物盒
